title: Distinct bridges meet only in the subgraph
statement: Let $H$ be a subgraph of a finite simple graph $G$, and let $e$ and $e'$ be edges of $G$ that do not belong to $H$, so both lie in $E(G)\setminus E(H)$. Recall that two such edges are called equivalent when they are joined by a walk, internally disjoint from $H$, whose first and last edges are the two given ones, and that the bridge of $H$ containing an edge $f$ is the subgraph of $G$ induced by the equivalence class of $f$. Write $B$ for the bridge containing $e$ and $B'$ for the bridge containing $e'$. If $e$ and $e'$ are not equivalent, then every vertex lying in both $B$ and $B'$ is a vertex of $H$; that is, $V(B)\cap V(B')\subseteq V(H)$.
hypotheses_covered: $e$ is an edge of $G$ not in $H$ (in $E(G)\setminus E(H)$)
$e'$ is an edge of $G$ not in $H$ (in $E(G)\setminus E(H)$)
$e$ and $e'$ are not related by the bridge equivalence (they lie in distinct bridges)
